title: If I had…: hypotheses
why: This lesson opens the unit on imagining and regretting with hypotheses: si + imparfait + conditional, to talk about what you would do with more time or money. It builds on the futur simple and the conditional of unit 11 and drills the golden rule: never the conditional after si.

Imagining: si + imparfait + conditional

In unit 11 you met two tools: si + present + future for real conditions (S'il fait beau, on ira à la plage), and the conditional for politeness and advice. Put them together and you can imagine: what would you do if you had more time, more money, another life?

ConditionTensesExample
real, possiblesi + present → futureSi j'ai le temps, je viendrai.
imagined, unlikely, unrealsi + imparfait → conditionalSi j'avais le temps, je viendrais.

The logic is the same as in English: \"If I have time, I'll come\" (it may happen) versus \"If I had time, I'd come\" (I probably don't). Even the tenses match: the English past after \"if\" becomes the French imparfait, and \"would\" becomes the conditional.

si + imparfaitconditional
jeSi j'avais le temps,je voyagerais.
tuSi tu avais le temps,tu voyagerais.
il / elle / onSi elle avait le temps,elle voyagerait.
nousSi nous avions le temps,nous voyagerions.
vousSi vous aviez le temps,vous voyageriez.
ils / ellesS'ils avaient le temps,ils voyageraient.

Si becomes s' only before il and ils: s'il, s'ils. Never before elle or on: si elle avait, si on partait.

", "

Never the conditional after si

This is the golden rule. In casual English you sometimes hear \"if I would have money…\", and learners translate it as \"si j'aurais\". In French, the conditional never goes in the si clause: si takes the imparfait, and the conditional goes in the other half of the sentence.

Si j'avais de l'argent, j'achèterais une maison à Nice.If I had money, I'd buy a house in Nice.

If I were…

English \"if I were\" is simply si j'étais: Si j'étais riche, je ne travaillerais plus. For advice, \"if I were you\" is usually à ta place or à votre place, followed by the conditional: À ta place, je refuserais.

Either order

The si clause can come first or second, with the same tenses: Je voyagerais plus si j'avais le temps. Use a comma only when si comes first.

Hear the r

The imparfait and the conditional share their endings. The only difference is the r of the future stem, so pronounce it clearly:

imparfaitconditional
je parlaisje parlerais
tu finissaistu finirais
il faisaitil ferait
nous pouvionsnous pourrions
ils étaientils seraient

Irregular verbs use their future stem in the conditional: ferais, serais, aurais, irais, pourrais, viendrais, voudrais, devrais, saurais, verrais.

", "

Dreams, wishes, suggestions

Si seulement… ! (if only…!)

On its own, si seulement + imparfait expresses a wish or a regret about the present: Si seulement j'avais plus de vacances ! Si seulement il faisait beau !

Et si… ? (how about…? what if…?)

Et si + imparfait makes a friendly suggestion, with no conditional at all. You know Si on allait au cinéma ? from unit 11: it's the same structure.

Et si on partait ce week-end ?How about going away this weekend?
Et si on invitait Thomas ?What if we invited Thomas?

Au cas où (in case)

To recognize: unlike si, au cas où is followed by the conditional: Prends un parapluie au cas où il pleuvrait. In conversation it often stands alone at the end: Prends un parapluie, au cas où.

Talking about your dreams

Useful phrases: gagner beaucoup d'argent, faire le tour du monde, prendre une année sabbatique, changer de métier, s'installer à la campagne, arrêter de travailler.

Si je prenais une année sabbatique, je m'installerais à la campagne et j'apprendrais à faire du pain.If I took a year off, I'd move to the countryside and learn to make bread.

To ask about someone's dreams: Qu'est-ce que tu ferais si… ? or, in casual speech, Tu ferais quoi si… ? The answer often keeps only the conditional: Moi ? Je partirais !
